To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a non‐linear model has been developed that accounts for large test mass angular deviations; the sequential acquisition of the OMS in accelerometer mode has been demonstrated; the angular requirements of the LTP are met in a time‐domain analysis; the LTP interferometry is ready for Drag‐Free system verification.
A non‐linear laser interferometer model for the LISA Pathfinder mission has been developed and successfully applied in a sequential acquisition approach.
a non‐linear model for the OMS is a valuable tool to verify the Drag‐Free System and that a sequential approach is possible to achieve interferometer acquisition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the verification of Drag‐Free System performance in development and real time testing environments.
the development of the LISA Pathfinder Optical Metrology System model and its use for Drag‐Free verification in development and in real‐time‐test scenarios.
the development of an accurate model of the LTP OMS and its use for Drag‐Free system verification in development and testing environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LTP interferometry is a very robust system and that it will be possible to acquire the interferometer in real‐time‐test environment.
the model has been successfully used to verify the LISA Drag‐Free System in development and real time testing environments.
the LTP Drag‐Free System is ready to be implemented and verified in the next phase of the LISA Pathfinder mission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LTP interferometric system can be acquired in a timely manner, even in the presence of the large angular deviations that are typical for Drag‐Free Systems.
the model has been successfully used to verify the Drag‐Free System performance and to demonstrate the interferometer acquisition in accelerometer mode.

the model is able to reproduce the LTP interferometry in all its complexity, including all the non‐linearities and non‐Gaussian noise sources, which are essential for a realistic Drag‐Free System test.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OMS is capable of acquiring a stable lock on the LISA Pathfinder test masses in a short time, which is crucial for Drag‐Free operations.
the OMS model can be used to verify Drag‐Free system performance, and that the model can be used in a sequential approach to acquisition.
the LTP OMS can be used for Drag‐Free mode acquisition, even if the LTP interferometers are not perfectly aligned with the spacecraft body axes.
